sentences.text: 2. The Tribunal has also come to the conclusion that the claimant had contributed to the extent of 20% to the accident and consequently, reduced the compensation to that extent.
The Tribunal has taken the view that the claimant had contributed to the accident on the ground that she was standing near the door and therefore, she had also contributed.
3. It is to be noticed here that the driver of the bus ought not to have moved the vehicle if the passenger was still near the door.
In that view of the matter, apportionment of negligence to the extent of 20% by the claimant cannot be sustained and the same is set aside.
4. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body, which is just and proper.
5. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2013, would be Rs.8,000/-.
6. As the claimant was aged 39 years, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,88,000/- (Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 15 x 20%) towards 'loss of future income'.
7.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.50,000/-
towards 'loss of future comfort and amenities in life'.

Since, the claimant was hospitalized for 12 days and suffered disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of future comfort and amenities in life'.

8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.43,000/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.7,000/-
towards 'incident expenses'.

In my view, since the claimant was hospitalized for 12 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'food, nourishment and other incidental expenses' as against Rs.7,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.43,000/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'food, nourishment and other incidental expenses'.
9.
The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as three months.

In my view, since the income is now taken at Rs.8,000/- per month, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.24,000/- (Rs.8,000/-
x 3) towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
